subject_matter: letters, theater, correspondence, writing, playwright, gossip, Hollywood, Bette Davis, Truman Capote, cats
description_block: Autograph Letter Signed and 24 Typed Letters Signed ("John"), 45 pp, most 4to, Hollywood, January 1, 1953 to December 15, 1957, to James Herlihy, mild to moderate toning throughout, with typed carbons of 11 of Herlihy's letters to Van Druten. 31 total items. A very writerly correspondence, each correspondent discussing his own work and that of the other, but also giving an overview of contemporary theater of the period.  Herlihy, the author of Midnight Cowboy , was an up-and-coming playwright and actor in the 1950s; Van Druten was a successful Broadway playwright and novelist, author of Leave Her to Heaven and Bell, Book and Candle. The two men struck up a correspondence in 1953 when the younger man wrote the older, and continued regularly until the week Van Druten died.   In his letters, Van Druten gives extensive and excellent notes on Herlihy's writing, and also passes on theater gossip: " Bette Davis has had an accident, fell down a flight of stairs in her house here, and is laid up in plaster or traction or whatnot, and so will NOT be doing LOOK HOMEWARD ANGEL after all." In a 1955 letter mentions his cat Pywacket (the name of the familiar in Bell, Book and Candle ) and also discusses his own work.  And in his last letter, he comments on the misadventures of Truman Capote: " Of course I read Truman Capote's article on Brando, and I agree that it was spiteful and vicious.  I had heard beforehand that there had been some trouble and they didn't want Truman around at all (who would?) so what Truman did was take Brando out for an evening and get him pretty drunk on not much liquor, and write down everything he said.  And the result, as you say, is easy and shabby and ridiculous, as a tape recording of anyone slightly drunk would probably be." See illustration.

description_block: Tsarouchis: The Face of Modern Greece. Los Angeles: Sylvester & Orphanos, 2004. 2 volumes. Vol one: [xxiv], 25, [18] pp.; Vol two: [4pp], 36 mounted color plates. Original boards and slipcase with beige cloth and red silk-screened portraits. Provenance : from the library of James Galanos. Signed first edition, signed by twenty-five contributors. Ralph Sylvester and Stathis Orphanos, booksellers and publishers produce elegant tributes to LGBTQ creatives. The current volume celebrates the life and work of gay artist Yannis Tsarouchis (1910-1989) and includes essays by Paul Cadmus, David Hockney, Horst, and Sir Stephen Spender. A pivotal figure in modern Greek art, Tsarouchis assimilated elements from Byzantine and folk art. Like many of his generation, he shunned the conservatism of the past and strove to create a style that would express a "Greek" aesthetic.

Extensive correspondence from Ray Bradbury to fellow science-fiction writer, Barry Harrington. Giving news of Bradbury's work in books and film, thanks for correspondence and exchanged books, etc. Includes a 1999 ALS with explanation of Bradbury's reluctance to work with Mel Gibson; a TLS from January 1984 (" Best in 1984. May it be a Harrington, not an Orwell, year! "); some advice to Harrington for his own writing: " you don't need to know the interworking of the industry, as you so badly put it. Interworkings, hell. Industry? Nuts. Write for yourself, as I said above. That's all you have. That's all you'll ever have ." In another note: " Novels are dangerous--you spend a lot of time and then what if don't sell?!?! Disaster! Write dozens of short stories! Chances are better to sell! "

subject_matter: photographs, stunt-pilot, flight log book, aviation, Lockheed, airfields, cockpits, P-38 Lightning, daredevil, test pilot
description_block: BURCHAM, MILO. 1903-1944.  A group of 69 photographs, most 8 x 10 inches, mostly gelatin silver prints with a few color, various sizes, 1930s-1940s, several with Lockheed Aviation stamps on verso, showing stunt-pilot Burcham in flight and on airfields. WITH: Flight log book, April 1927-April 1940, 108 pp, 12mo; and miscellaneous related material, including the flight log of Milo Burcham, Jr. Famed daredevil test pilot Milo Burcham set a world record for flying upside-down that lasted nearly six decades. He was Lockheed Aviation's Chief Pilot in England and later their Chief Engineering Pilot in America and was involved in developing their P-38 Lightning fighter plane. Burcham died in a fiery crash at Lockheed Air Terminal while testing the YP-80 Shooting Star and posthumously received the Citation for the Air Medal from Franklin D. Roosevelt. Burcham's log book records his flights over a 13 year period, most of them in Lockheed planes, flown mainly between Los Angeles and various major Southwestern cities, and includes brief remarks about many of the flights. The photographs in this lot primarily feature Burcham during his heyday in the late 1930s and early 1940s, posing with planes (including many with his P-38, Yipee ), on airfields, and in cockpits.

subject_matter: rocket, NASA, Northrop, lifting body, thruster, aircraft, alloys, plastic nozzle, flight control, aerospace engineering
description_block: ORIGINAL THRUSTER ROCKET FOR JOINT NASA/NORTHROP LIFTING BODY PROJECT. Various alloys with plastic nozzle, 8 3/4 inches tall, 1967-1973, with NASA Flight Research Center tag and receipt. The M2-F3 (M for Manned, F for Flight) lifting body aircraft was a joint project of Northrup along with the engineers at NASA's Flight Research Center, Ames Research Center and the Air Force. The lifting body is essentially a wingless aircraft that used the lift provided by the fuselage shape and would allow the pilot to land in a horizontal mode — a concept that was to aid the spacecraft of the future. The M2-F3 was a rebuild of the earlier M2-F2 which had crashed in May 1967. Among the additions on the updated vehicle was a reaction control system which utilized thrusters, such as the present example, to provide attitude control and sometimes translation. It was a system similar to that of orbiting spacecraft and was likely borrowed from that realm. The vehicle made 27 flights before it was donated to the Smithsonian Institution in December 1973.

description_block: Wood, pokerwork Heights 17 3/4 and 18in (45 and 45.5cm) Provenance Collected by an Belgium officer in 1907 Ch. Aubrechts Collection, Lasne Damien Reeners Collection, Brussels Aguttes, Paris, 20 November 2009, Lot 299 Private Princely Collection Literature Beaulieux, Dick, Belgium Collects African Art , Arts and Applications, Brussels, 2000, p. 291 Mangbetu figurative sculpture of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries portray the idealized beauty of the Mangbetu. They appear to have been carved for the appreciation of chiefs and other elite individuals, often with names carved on them, as with the female presented here. Each with naturalistic facial features, muscular legs, arms and hands resting on the stomach, large necks and squared shoulders; the male with a conical hat and appearing to wear western clothes; the female with a distinctive elaborate Mangbetu coiffure, enhanced buttocks and pointed breasts; "ZOWAI" incised on the underside of her right foot, "ISSAVI" on the underside of her left; fine light brown patina.
